objective: Independent cross-provider safety review of the new QuantPilot paper execution path

receipt.summary: Independent safety review of the frozen quantpilot/paper snapshot: VERDICT = BLOCK. Six P1 defects confirmed with file+line evidence, three of them reproduced by executing the code offline. Highest impact: (1) the 5-minute execution lease is never renewed and is orphaned by any crash or partial begin(), so runtime.cycle() aborts at broker.begin() (runtime.py:49) before the position-protection loop (runtime.py:74) for up to 5 minutes after every restart - reproduced against PaperStateStore; (2) broker.py:111-116 reimplements cancel-identity verification inline, dropping 6 guards present in the reviewed paper_kill.py:541-582 reference (forwarding org number, business date, original_order_number, total_filled_quantity/amount equality, cancelable_quantity>0, exchange_id) and turning the routine "filled before cancel" race into a hard raise that aborts the whole cycle before protection; it also cannot detect external working orders on the shared account; (3) store.control() lets `pause` silently override an in-progress `flatten`, after which `resume` re-enables entries with positions still open and no status flag records the abandoned liquidation - reproduced; (4) the fail-closed reconciliation states (account_position_mismatch, dispatch_missing, broker_reconciliation_blocked) have no CLI remediation path and permanently deny protective exits to any position the ledger does not know about; (5) a single missing minute permanently disqualifies a symbol for the rest of the session via the durable bars table + validate_bars gap rejection, surfaced only as one audit row - reproduced; (6) the entire 13-module order-submitting package has zero test coverage. P2 items cover an unclamped AI score at runtime.py:114 that halts entries under a misleading incident code, capital isolation resting on a single SQLite integer while the kernel's broker-cash guard is fed a non-binding experiment-relative reserve, cost-basis values recorded as market prices in durable dispatch evidence, a balance/fills snapshot ordering mismatch, and an unused endpoint added to the client allowlist. Default-disabled state, secret handling, and the partial-fill cumulative-replay invariant all pass. No edits, no network, no credentials read; working tree unchanged.

criteria.criterion: Independent safety verdict with concrete failure scenarios and exact code locations
criteria.evidence: Verdict BLOCK. 6 P1 + 5 P2 findings delivered, each anchored to file:line (e.g. broker.py:34/111-116, runtime.py:49/74/114, store.py:113/130-134, cli.py:60, paper_kill.py:541-582, paper_submission.py:459-472). Three P1 findings and one P2 finding were reproduced by executing the code offline rather than inferred: the 5-minute lease conflict window (+10s/+60s/+299s all PaperStateConflictError), the validate_bars whole-batch gap rejection, the flatten->pause->resume control-state loss, and the AI score blend raising ValueError at 1.72.

criteria.criterion: No edits, no network or secrets
criteria.evidence: git status --porcelain=v1 at the end is byte-identical to the start (' M quantpilot/packages/core/kis_paper.py', '?? quantpilot/jobs/check_kis_paper_connection.py', '?? quantpilot/paper/'); filesChanged is empty. All probe scripts were heredocs writing only into %TEMP% (qp_review_*, qp_review2_*, qp_review3_*), and .pyc output is gitignored per .gitignore:4. No broker, Slack, or KIS call was made - only PaperStateStore/Store SQLite and pure functions were exercised. No .env, token, or credential file was read; .env*, .claude, .codex, .agents were never opened.

findings.evidence: begin() opens a session with lease_expires_at=now+5min (broker.py:34) and nothing in quantpilot/paper ever renews it. If DurablePaperSubmissionCoordinator(...) (broker.py:35) or expire_stale_prepared_dispatches() (broker.py:36) raises, self.session is already set but runtime.py:49's begun=True has not executed, so the finally at runtime.py:136 skips end() and the row stays 'active'. A SIGKILL has the same effect. Reproduced against PaperStateStore: 'restart at +10s -> begin() FAILS: PaperStateConflictError: an unexpired paper execution session already owns the store', same at +60s and +299s, first success at +301s. gateway.begin() is the first statement inside cycle()'s try (runtime.py:49); the position-protection loop is at runtime.py:74.
findings.proposal: Size the lease to the cycle (e.g. cycle_seconds*3) instead of a fixed 5 minutes, wrap broker.begin() so that any failure after start_paper_execution_session immediately calls close_paper_execution_session and clears self.session, and set begun=True as soon as the session row exists so the finally always attempts release.

findings.evidence: broker.py:111-115 reimplements cancel-identity matching inline and checks only order_number, order_branch_number, symbol, side, order_quantity, order_price, order_time and order_division_code=='00'. The reviewed reference _cancel_identity_matches (paper_kill.py:556-582) additionally requires broker_forwarding_order_org_number, broker_business_date == business_date, original_order_number in {'','0'}, row.total_filled_quantity == int(dispatch.cumulative_filled_quantity), Decimal(row.total_filled_amount) == sum(fill_evidence notional), row.cancelable_quantity == int(quantity - cumulative_filled) > 0, and row.exchange_id == 'KRX'. Dropping the two fill-state equalities lets broker.py POST a cancel for an order whose broker-side fill state has already advanced past the durable evidence. Separately broker.py:116 raises cancel_identity_unverified whenever len(matches)!=1, which is the normal outcome when the order filled between the reconcile at runtime.py:50 and the cancel at runtime.py:71 (different KIS endpoints, >=1.05s apart via LimitedTransport); that call sits in the bare cycle body, so one routine race aborts the cycle before the protection loop at runtime.py:74. The reference treats the same condition as a reason string ('external_working_order_detected', paper_kill.py:271-274), not an exception. broker.py also iterates dispatch->rows, so unmanaged working orders belonging to another party on the shared paper account are never detected.
findings.proposal: Call paper_kill._cancel_identity_matches (or export it) instead of the inline predicate; iterate rows->dispatches so external working orders are surfaced; and treat 'no cancelable row' as a no-op that defers to the reconciler, wrapping the runtime.py:68-71 loop per order so no single cancel can skip position protection.

findings.evidence: control() at store.py:113 only rejects 'start'/'resume' while control=='flattening'; 'pause' is allowed through and overwrites the state. Reproduced: after control('flatten') state is 'flattening'; control('pause') yields 'paused'; control('resume') then yields 'running'. Once state leaves 'flattening', runtime.py:79's reason expression no longer emits 'flatten', so liquidation stops, and runtime.py:86-88 never writes the flatten_completed audit. reporting.snapshot() (reporting.py:20-26) exposes only 'control', so status output after the pause is indistinguishable from a normal pause and the operator cannot see that the liquidation was abandoned while positions are still open.
findings.proposal: Store the flatten intent as an independent durable flag rather than a value of 'control', so pause/resume are orthogonal to it; keep liquidating while the flag is set, refuse resume until it clears, and surface it in snapshot() (e.g. flatten_pending: true).

findings.evidence: reconcile() raises dispatch_missing (broker.py:52), account_position_mismatch (broker.py:62) and broker_reconciliation_blocked (broker.py:63). All three propagate from runtime.py:50, which is above the position-protection loop at runtime.py:74, so every subsequent cycle returns {'status':'blocked'} without ever placing a protective exit. The CLI subcommand set (cli.py:63-66: status, pause, resume, flatten, report, strategies, start, worker, config) contains no command that can acknowledge or adopt a divergence, and config --set data_mode is rejected by store.py:99 whenever self.orders() is non-empty (all orders, not just open ones). A position that exists at the broker but not in the ledger - e.g. a fill reported by KIS after the local order was already marked terminal 'cancelled', or any pre-existing holding on the shared paper account at first start - is therefore permanently unprotected with no in-product recovery path.
findings.proposal: Add an explicit operator command that records an acknowledged divergence (adopt the broker position into the ledger, or quarantine it) with an audit entry, and move the reconcile call so a reconciliation block still allows protective exits for positions the ledger does know about.

findings.evidence: validate_bars raises 'gap within trading session' if any two same-date bars are not exactly one minute apart (strategy.py:133-134). Reproduced: a contiguous 5-bar batch returns 5 bars, while the same batch missing minute 3 raises ValueError for the whole batch. Bars are durable (store.py:194-202 bars table) and load_bars returns all of today's rows (store.py:204-210), so the gap never heals. Gaps arise routinely: runtime.py:94 rotates the universe every 300s while market.minutes only returns the recent window, so any symbol absent for longer than that window and then re-selected has a permanent hole; the same applies to a zero-trade minute or a single failed fetch. The failure is caught at runtime.py:106-107 and recorded as one candidate_unavailable audit row; reporting.snapshot() exposes no candidate-failure count, so an operator sees {'status':'running','signals':0} while most of the universe is permanently disqualified.
findings.proposal: Either allow bounded gaps in validate_bars (treat a missing minute as a no-trade minute for indicator purposes) or evaluate only the contiguous suffix ending at the latest bar; and surface a per-cycle candidate_failed count in snapshot() so silent universe collapse is observable.

findings.evidence: grep -rn "quantpilot\.paper\." quantpilot/tests/ returns no matches. The 13-module package is classified critical risk and submits real orders through DurablePaperSubmissionCoordinator, yet no unit or integration test exercises broker.KisGateway, runtime.Runtime, store.Store, risk.authorize_order or cli.main. The existing paper tests (test_paper_submission_coordinator.py, test_paper_reconciliation.py, test_paper_kill_persistence.py) cover the kernel beneath the adapter and never traverse it. Every P1 above is reachable by a small deterministic test with an injected clock and a fake client, which is direct evidence the gap is causal.
findings.proposal: Add unit tests with an injected clock and fake KIS client covering at minimum: restart with an unexpired lease, cancel when the order has left the cancelable list, partial fill then cancel replay, flatten interrupted by pause, reconcile position divergence, and a cycle where the bar history contains a gap.

findings.evidence: runtime.py:114 computes replace(s, score=.8*s.score+.2*ai.candidate_scores.get(s.symbol, s.score)) with no bound on the model-supplied value. Reproduced: score 0.9 blended with an AI value of 5.0 gives 1.72 and Signal.__post_init__ raises ValueError('signal score must be between zero and one'). That propagates to cycle()'s except at runtime.py:131, which alerts execution_reconciliation_required - a broker-reconciliation incident code for what is actually bad model output - and sets the incident that blocks entries at runtime.py:89. Because the assessment is persisted in settings (jobs.py:32) the failure repeats every cycle until it goes stale. The asymmetry is explicit: allocate_weights defensively validates ai_scores through _valid_unit_score (strategy.py:431-434), the same file's line 114 does not.
findings.proposal: Clamp or discard the AI candidate score at runtime.py:114 the way allocate_weights does (drop non-finite or out-of-[0,1] values), and use a distinct incident code such as assessment_rejected so the operator is not told to reconcile the broker.

findings.evidence: broker.py:101 passes minimum_cash_reserve=max(0., snapshot.cash - notional*(1+fee)) where snapshot.cash is the 5,000,000 experiment ledger (broker.py:79). paper_submission.py:459-472 subtracts that value from the broker's own orderable cash: broker_cash_krw = min(orderable_cash, no_receivable_buy_amount) - minimum_cash_reserve_krw, then rejects if quantity*limit_price > broker_cash_krw. With a ~100M KRW paper account the subtraction of a ~4M reserve leaves the guard non-binding for every order the experiment can size, so the kernel's independent broker-cash check provides no second line of defence and isolation rests entirely on the settings.cash integer in one SQLite file. cli.py:60 makes the runtime directory a free CLI argument and process_lock is per-directory (cli.py:97), so a second invocation with a different --runtime-dir creates a fresh 5,000,000 ledger and a fresh broker.sqlite3 against the same KIS account; the account_binding check at broker.py:27 is per-store and passes. Combined exposure becomes N x 5M; the account_position_mismatch check at broker.py:62 only trips after the first fill, wedging both processes rather than preventing the over-allocation.
findings.proposal: Derive minimum_cash_reserve from the broker's own orderable cash (reserve = broker_orderable_cash - experiment_remaining_cash) so the kernel guard actually binds the experiment to its slice, and enforce an account-scoped singleton (a lock keyed on account_scope_fingerprint rather than on the runtime directory).

findings.evidence: broker.py:80 builds PortfolioPosition(market_price=p['basis']/p['quantity']) - the average acquisition cost, not a market price - and broker.py:78 computes equity as cash + sum(basis). That snapshot is persisted into the durable dispatch as snapshot_equity, snapshot_daily_loss_ratio and snapshot_monthly_loss_ratio (paper_submission.py:525-530) under source='paper_experiment_reconciled' (broker.py:81). Live marks are available and used elsewhere in the same package - runtime.equity() at runtime.py:178-180 and reporting.snapshot() at reporting.py:14 both read store.get('marks') - so the cost-basis choice is not a data-availability constraint. The consequence is that the durable audit record's loss ratios can never reflect unrealised drawdown.
findings.proposal: Use store.get('marks') for market_price and equity in the dispatch snapshot, falling back to cost basis only for symbols with no mark, and label the source accordingly (e.g. paper_experiment_marked vs paper_experiment_cost_basis).

findings.evidence: reconcile_unresolved calls self._client.get_balance(...) at paper_reconciliation.py:107 and only then get_daily_orders_and_fills at :110-115, so broker_balance is strictly older than the fill data. broker.py:46 captures that balance, broker.py:47-59 applies the newer fills to the local ledger, and broker.py:60-62 then compares the freshly updated local positions for exact equality against the older remote snapshot. A fill landing between the two KIS calls therefore appears in local but not remote and raises account_position_mismatch, which per finding P1-no-remediation-for-fail-closed-states aborts the cycle before the protection loop. It self-heals on the next cycle but each occurrence costs one cycle of protective coverage and raises an operator incident.
findings.proposal: Compare local positions against the balance as of the balance timestamp (i.e. exclude fills whose evidence_at is later than broker_balance's capture time), or re-fetch the balance after applying fills before asserting equality.

findings.evidence: The diff adds KIS_DAILY_PRICE_ENDPOINT = '/uapi/domestic-stock/v1/quotations/inquire-daily-price' and inserts it into _ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS. grep -rn 'KIS_DAILY_PRICE_ENDPOINT|inquire-daily-price' across quantpilot/ returns only these two definition lines - no caller exists anywhere in the tree, including quantpilot/paper. The other two additions (inquire-time-itemchartprice, volume-rank) are used by data.py:63 and data.py:84.
findings.proposal: Remove the inquire-daily-price constant and its allowlist entry until a caller exists; the allowlist is a security boundary and should not widen ahead of use.

unresolvedRisks: quantpilot/jobs/check_kis_paper_connection.py is new and untracked, and cli.build_runtime (cli.py:41) imports connection_config from it to construct the KIS client, but quantpilot/jobs is outside the allowed scope so I did not review it. The credential-loading boundary that feeds KisPaperClient is therefore unverified.

data.py:48 parses stck_bsop_date+stck_cntg_hour into a bar START timestamp. inquire-time-itemchartprice was only just added to the endpoint allowlist so there is no prior art in this repository for whether KIS labels these rows by bar start or bar end. If they are end timestamps, _opening_range_signal's exact session_open+0..14 lookup (strategy.py:241-245) can never match and the opening_range_breakout strategy would silently never fire. This cannot be settled offline.

Throughput was not measured. LimitedTransport enforces ~1.05s between every authentication, quote, minute-bar, order and reconciliation call (data.py:21-32), while policy.cycle_seconds defaults to 10 and max_candidates to 20. Twenty minute-bar fetches alone consume ~21s, so real cycle duration almost certainly exceeds cycle_seconds; the interaction with the 5-minute lease (finding P1-lease-orphan-protection-gap) under a slow network was not quantified.

With the default slack_enabled=False, jobs.work_once (jobs.py:10, :44) never drains the outbox, so incident alerts enqueued by runtime.alert (runtime.py:26) are persisted but never delivered. Incidents remain discoverable via snapshot()['incident'], but there is no push path in the default configuration.

The project's own verification commands (python -m pytest quantpilot/tests, npm run test/build) were not run. This was a read-only review that changed nothing, and running pytest would have created .pytest_tmp artifacts in the worktree that the change guard checks; the task-specified verification command was run instead and passed.
